nodes.label: Nine-stage study pipeline
nodes.rationale: Each stage names what it reads, what it writes, and what it will refuse to do, so a reader can tell a break from a change without running the code.

nodes.label: Stage 1 — ingest (immutable Stage 1 artifacts)
nodes.rationale: Do not re-run casually: re-running changes the vintage, and §12 forbids comparing numbers across vintages. --end is exclusive and clip_to_window() enforces it.

nodes.label: Stage 2 — segments and the window budget
nodes.rationale: The assertion is exact equality per origin, never against the pooled 4.9%: asserted pooled it fires spuriously at fourteen of fifteen origins, gets loosened until it passes, and then can no longer distinguish positional drift from ordinary between-origin variation.

nodes.label: Stage 3 — the twelve per-bar variates
nodes.rationale: 75,091 usable bars produce 75,062 feature rows; the 29 dropped rows are one per segment because r is computed per segment. No variate uses a rolling window, which makes the center=True leak class unrepresentable.

nodes.label: Stage 3b — effective dimensionality and the gate
nodes.rationale: Gate PR at K=8 measures 4.393 < 5.0 so the gate does not pass; the prescribed action is disclosure, not a ladder re-cut, because D01 establishes there is no second consistent cut over F1-F5.

nodes.label: Stage 4 — pre-flight invariants
nodes.rationale: Three checks, each of which failed the first time it ran: scale invariance MSE(c*x)/c^2 == MSE(x), single-batch overfit at dropout=0.0, and Naive-RW mapped as y_z = -mu_g/sigma_g.

nodes.label: Stage 5 — the pilot gate, judged on validation
nodes.rationale: Judged on the validation sub-block, never on test: §11 requires test blocks be opened once after the design is frozen, and a gate that repositions the title on a test-block result cannot coexist with that. Twelve cells are ordinary main-grid run_ids so Stage 6 skips them.

nodes.label: Stage 6 — the 534-run grid
nodes.rationale: 582 nominal cells minus 48 that are literally the same run: the horizon sweep's H=24 slice at seeds 42-44 shares run_ids with the main grid, and run_id is the identity of a run.

nodes.label: Stage 7 — evaluation of RQ1, RQ2, RQ3
nodes.rationale: Four things easy to get wrong are handled for the caller: order of operations on ratios, error bars bound to aggregation level, beta1's effective n, and a restricted studentized bootstrap.

nodes.label: Stage 8 — save paper_numbers.json
nodes.rationale: Every table and figure in the manuscript is generated from that file, never transcribed.

nodes.label: The notebook carries the package (twelve %%writefile cells)
nodes.rationale: A Kaggle session needs only the notebook and BTCUSDT_1h.parquet, so the repository is never uploaded. The notebook asserts the imported itransformer_btc lives in its own working directory, because two copies of the code with one stale is the failure the assertion exists to catch.

nodes.label: tools/build_notebook.py — notebook generator
nodes.rationale: Sits outside the package on purpose: it is build tooling, not study logic, and nothing under src/ may import it. Hand-editing a package cell in the notebook is a defect the next generator run reverts silently.

nodes.label: tests/test_notebook_sync.py — byte-identity assertion
nodes.rationale: Pays down the cost of a duplicated ~4,000-line copy: editing src/ without regenerating fails the suite.

nodes.label: Package module inventory and per-module guarantees
nodes.rationale: Each module is listed with the one guarantee it enforces, so a guarantee has a single owner: config derives the grid, splits raises on purge violation, model returns the target channel alone, runner shards the full manifest.

nodes.label: run_id — deterministic run identity
nodes.rationale: {model}_o{origin:02d}_K{K:02d}_H{H:03d}_s{seed}. Changing any component deliberately orphans prior outputs rather than silently reusing a mismatched result.

nodes.label: artifacts/preds/{run_id}.parquet schema
nodes.rationale: timestamp is the window start, not the forecast origin. Since L=96 is a multiple of 24, hour-of-day is preserved, which is what makes the 00:00 UTC non-overlapping phase selectable by timestamp // 3.6e6 % 24 == 0.

nodes.label: artifacts/meta/{run_id}.json schema
nodes.rationale: Carries git_sha, code_sha256, input_parquet, input_sha256, input_sha256_source, mu_g, sigma_g, naive_rw_z and status, so every number resolves to a code identity and an input vintage.

nodes.label: code_sha256 — code identity where git is absent
nodes.rationale: git_sha is "unknown" on Kaggle because there is no git repository there, so the digest of the package source with line endings normalised is what identifies the code §12 requires every number to resolve to.

nodes.label: input_sha256_source — report vs file-digest provenance
nodes.rationale: "report" when the digest came from the Stage 1 report beside the artifact, "file-digest" when the parquet was hashed directly; both are correct, and stating which is what makes the number checkable.

nodes.label: Two window semantics — contained vs origin
nodes.rationale: Train/validation use "contained" because the H-step target may not cross the boundary; test blocks use "origin" because §8.3 licenses the 96-bar lookback reaching back and blocking it would make evaluation unrealistically pessimistic. The two differ by exactly L+H-1 = 119 windows.

nodes.label: GPU-resident batching, no Dataset or DataLoader
nodes.rationale: At ~280k parameters the run is dominated by data movement and Python overhead, which a per-item loader maximises — roughly 10x worse, which puts the grid outside the 30 h weekly quota outright. nn.DataParallel is rejected because at batch 32 scatter/gather costs more than the split saves.

nodes.label: Two GPUs are two independent processes, not two threads
nodes.rationale: torch.manual_seed seeds every CUDA device, so two threads seeding concurrently would clobber each other's generator mid-run and §12's reproducibility contract would be unenforceable. One process per GPU with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES pinned gives each worker its own global RNG, interpreter lock and crash isolation.

nodes.label: Four grid arms — main, uniform, fresh, horizon
nodes.rationale: main 300 (itr_), uniform 75 (itru_, attention forced uniform), fresh 15 (itrf_, one per origin at o_i+90d), horizon 144 (itr_, minus the 48 shared cells).

nodes.label: Session budget guard checked at run boundaries
nodes.rationale: Bounds the session, not the worker: Kaggle's 12 h wall starts at cell 0, so the ~20-25 min prelude is subtracted before workers get their budget. Hitting the wall interactively loses /kaggle/working entirely, so the margin is not somewhere to be approximate.

nodes.label: Evaluation cells gated on GRID_COMPLETE
nodes.rationale: A partial grid is an unbalanced panel and §9.1's estimators refuse one by design. Partial evaluation is never offered as a fallback, because a half-panel beta1 is a different estimand, not a noisier one.

nodes.label: Kaggle session chaining and glob-based resume
nodes.rationale: Roots are discovered by glob over /kaggle/input/*/preds and /kaggle/input/*/*/preds, never by dataset slug, so the Dataset's name and nesting do not matter. A run is complete only when both artifacts exist and meta.status == "complete".

nodes.label: Column order is ladder order (K = first K columns)
nodes.rationale: Rung K is exactly the first K columns and r is channel 0 at every rung, so the target channel index never depends on the rung.

nodes.label: Feature frame — 75,062 rows, 29 dropped one per segment
Ratio metrics from seed-averaged MSEs, never averaged ratios
nodes.rationale: The two differ by Jensen, and the second would require pairing seed 42 at K=1 with seed 42 at K=8 — independent runs of different models where any of 5! orderings gives a different answer.

nodes.label: Error bar bound to the aggregation level
nodes.rationale: Per-cell means mean ± std across seeds; anything aggregated across origins means SE across origins, with seed std reported separately as a Monte-Carlo diagnostic. Reporting seed std on an aggregated row understates headline uncertainty by roughly an order of magnitude.

nodes.label: beta1's effective n is the cluster count, bounded near 4
nodes.rationale: On a balanced panel with origin fixed effects beta1-hat reduces algebraically to the mean of the origin-specific within-slopes, so inference is a one-sample test on G = 15 numbers, and effective independence is bounded near 4 by the 79.2% training-window overlap between consecutive origins.

nodes.label: Restricted studentized one-sided wild cluster bootstrap, B = 99,999
nodes.rationale: Both Rademacher and Webb weights reported with the more conservative as the headline; the p-value floors at 1/(B+1) because no finite bootstrap supports a literal zero.

nodes.label: Clark–West, not Diebold–Mariano, at the Stage 5 gate
nodes.rationale: K=1's feature set is a strict subset of K=8's under the same architecture and sample, so the pair is nested and standard DM is systematically undersized against exactly the alternative being tested.

nodes.label: Expected numbers table — tell a break from a change
nodes.rationale: Pins 75,094 bars / 3 unusable, 75,062 feature rows, 15 origins, 70.12 MB largest tensor, 280,472 parameters, gate PR 4.393, and the first measured run's RelMSE 1.0183 / R2_oos -0.0183.

nodes.label: What is not built yet
nodes.rationale: Stated plainly because a reader should not have to discover it by running: comparison baselines (~255 runs), the economic evaluation, the optional K=16 rung, and a confirmed T4 timing. RQ1-RQ3 are answerable without the baselines because Naive-RW is computed from the scaler.

nodes.label: Named dependency extras — core, train, ingest, stats, dev
nodes.rationale: The core set is the data plane only so each dependency's reason is visible rather than ambient; pandas sits behind ingest and stats, never in core, which would make the §2 exemption ambient.

nodes.label: data/raw is never written to
nodes.rationale: Four Stage 1 artifacts live there and are immutable; every derived thing goes to data/processed/ or artifacts/.

nodes.label: Troubleshooting table — symptom, cause, fix
nodes.rationale: Several rows deliberately answer "do not loosen the assertion": a purge failure is a real leak, an unbalanced panel must be finished not approximated, and a result that looks too good is leakage until proven otherwise.
